propositions: Current clarity scoring rewards volume and generic shape (any H2, length thresholds, any bullet) rather than conformance to documented plan-writing guidance and per-ticket-type required sections.
Clarity checks are duplicated across two code locations inviting measurement drift and inconsistency.

Deterministic checks can validate required-section presence keyed on graph altitude, per-AC verification coverage linking to proving methods, placeholder-free executable Scope/Approach, grounded file edits, AC text hygiene, and Testing shape when declared—without requiring subjective semantic judgments.
Author guide and authoritative criteria conflict on Success Criteria (containers) and rejected-alternative requirements, causing ambiguity in what clarity should enforce.

Recommended additions must be mechanically testable via text parsing and structural rules, with clear false-positive controls, rather than adding more scale points to a system where filler compensates for missing required sections.
